signals.title: AUD/CHF — G10 Bilateral Theme + Geopolitical Shock
signals.text: AUD/CHF trades at 0.5613 amid acute global risk aversion sparked by multiple oil tanker mine explosions east of the Strait of Hormuz. On the 1W G10 Currency Strength Scorecard, CHF leads all peers at +1.257% across 6 pairs, while AUD lags at -2.229% across 4 pairs, generating a wide 3.486% bilateral spread. The safe-haven CHF bid completely overrides AUD's carry premium, which sits at +485bp nominally (RBA 4.85% vs SNB 0.00%). With VIX elevated at 25.6, flow dynamics heavily favor capital preservation over carry returns. Downside momentum in AUD remains reinforced by an active downtrend across broader dollar pairs. Trade bias: Bearish AUD/CHF; safe-haven flows dominate carry yield. Catalyst: RBA meeting 8 Dec — hike bias active. Risk: De-escalation headlines in the Persian Gulf trigger an aggressive carry squeeze back toward 0.5750.

signals.title: USD/JPY — Options Skew + Strait of Hormuz Disruption
signals.text: USD/JPY prints at 158.34, holding above its SMA20 of 157.96 and SMA50 of 157.30 while testing the SMA200 resistance near 158.56. Escalating military actions in the Strait of Hormuz have pushed WTI to $90.8 and elevated VIX to 25.6, driving demand for downside protection. The 1M 25-delta Risk Reversals print an extreme put skew of -1.97, while 1M implied volatility trades at 6.9% against a 30-day realized volatility of 4.9%, yielding an elevated 2.0% volatility risk premium. Despite a supportive nominal rate differential favoring USD by +275bp (Fed 4.00% vs BoJ 1.25%), the options market is paying up heavily for downside protection as the pair trades below the 160.00 intervention threshold. Trade bias: Bearish USD/JPY, downside protection demand surging. Catalyst: BoJ Summary of Opinions at 23:50 UTC. Risk: Spot acceptance above 160.00 invalidates the downside hedging structure.

signals.title: EUR/USD — Crowded Speculative Short + Retail Divergence
signals.text: EUR/USD trades at 1.1142, maintaining an established downtrend below its falling SMA20 at 1.1195 and SMA50 at 1.1347. Leveraged funds hold a heavy net short position of -104,030 contracts (CFTC, week ending Nov 3), ranking at the 2nd percentile of its 52-week range (z = -1.80) after extending shorts by 4,473 contracts WoW. Conversely, Retail sentiment data retail sentiment registers an extreme 85% long positioning, setting up a sharp institutional vs retail divergence. Meanwhile, US 5Y yields fell 19bp over the trailing 5 sessions (FRED, as of Nov 5), driven primarily by a 21bp contraction in breakevens. Trade bias: Bearish EUR/USD; institutional trend and carry favor downside despite retail contrarian long crowding. Catalyst: US CPI on 10 Nov — forecast 4.2% y/y. Risk: Daily close above the SMA20 at 1.1195 sparks short covering toward the SMA50.

signals.title: USD/CAD — Macro Divergence + Trend Breakout
signals.text: USD/CAD trades at 1.4116, executing a bullish expansion bar on the daily session that places spot firmly above its SMA20 (1.4069), SMA50 (1.4043), and SMA200 (1.3890). The rally is supported by starkly diverging macroeconomic fundamentals, highlighted by October US non-farm payrolls adding +165k jobs against an expected +65k, while Canadian employment contracted by -4.7k with unemployment rising to 6.7% (a 3.00-sigma miss). The Fed-BoC policy differential grants the USD a +150bp nominal carry advantage (Fed 4.00% vs BoC 2.50%). Leveraged funds remain net short CAD at -85,289 contracts, yet short-covering of +11,663 contracts WoW suggests speculative positioning is adjusting to policy divergence. Trade bias: Bullish USD/CAD; labor divergence reinforces carry dominance. Catalyst: BoC meeting 9 Dec — hike bias active. Risk: Decisive break back below the SMA20 support at 1.4069 invalidates near-term upside momentum.
